title: Extract valid Network fracture-set samples for generation
description: Implement the minimal source-data boundary for the Network-based PorePy generator. Work in fractopo/interop/porepy.py and add focused tests in tests/interop/test_porepy.py. Do not make PorePy a dependency. Network is the sole v1 source. Read only Network.trace_data: azimuth_set_array, azimuth_array, length_array and Network.azimuth_set_names. A usable observation has a named non-NULL_SET azimuth-set label, finite trace azimuth, finite strictly positive length, and finite dip in [0, 90] from network.trace_gdf["dip"]. Exclude every unusable observation and entire named sets with zero usable observations. Set proportions are counts of usable observations, normalized across remaining sets; do not use length weighting. Raise ValueError naming the cause if no usable set remains. Return the smallest private structure the exporter needs: per-set aligned azimuth/dip/length arrays or row indices plus normalized count proportions. Do not retain or validate dip_direction: v1 derives right-hand-rule dip direction from sampled strike implicitly and PorePy CSV has no dip-direction field. Keep helpers pure, private, and local to porepy.py; no new public data class or abstraction.
acceptance_criteria: Tests construct a minimal Network with named sets and a dip trace column. Tests prove: (1) valid rows are grouped by named set with aligned azimuth/dip/length values; (2) NULL_SET, missing/non-finite/out-of-range dip, non-finite azimuth, and non-positive/non-finite length rows are excluded; (3) proportions use usable-row counts and sum to 1; (4) an all-invalid input raises a useful ValueError; (5) manual and automatic Network set labels work because extraction consumes Network.trace_data labels. Do not add a dip_direction input/column test. Run nix develop -c pytest tests/interop/test_porepy.py -q. Run nix develop -c prek run --all-files. Before closing: br close with test evidence, br sync --flush-only, git add -f .beads/issues.jsonl plus source/test files, and commit --no-gpg-sign with this bead id.

title: Generate PorePy 3D circular-fracture populations from Network data
description: Epic tracking the first Network-based random PorePy 3D circular-fracture exporter. Scope is deliberately empirical rather than a general statistical-modelling framework: Network supplies manual/automatic set labels, trace azimuths and lengths; trace_gdf supplies dip. Decisions: use usable-observation count proportions; exclude invalid/unassigned observations and renormalize; sample valid rows empirically with replacement; generated strike comes from trace azimuth; right-hand-rule dip direction is implicit; caller injects optional numpy.random.Generator; domain is emitted by default; centres only must be in cuboid; PorePy semi-axis is trace length / 2; all current 3D exporters are corrected likewise. Keep PorePy optional/non-dependency. Parametric/von-Mises orientation sampling, fitted-length sampling, dip_direction input columns, full-disk containment, column overrides, CLI/UI work, CSV validator API, and intersection conditioning are out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: Close only after children 861, zud, w0b, and hkc are closed; the focused test file, full test suite, pre-commit/lint, and documentation build (only if non-autodoc docs changed) have passed; and the work is committed. Verify br dep cycles --json remains empty, br sync --flush-only has run, .beads/issues.jsonl is forcibly staged because .beads is ignored, and git status is clean.

title: Export seeded random circular fractures from a Network into PorePy 3D CSV
description: After 861 and zud close, implement one public exporter in fractopo/interop/porepy.py, with unit tests in tests/interop/test_porepy.py. Suggested name: export_network_to_porepy_3d_csv_format; choose an equally explicit established-style name only if necessary. Inputs: a fractopo.analysis.network.Network, positive integer fracture_count, cuboid bounds in exact order (xmin, ymin, zmin, xmax, ymax, zmax), and optional numpy.random.Generator. No integer seed overload and no global np.random state. Reuse 861 extraction. Given usable sets in Network.azimuth_set_names order, compute quotas with largest-remainder allocation: raw = proportion * fracture_count; take floors; allocate remaining count(s) to greatest fractional remainder; resolve equal remainders by original azimuth_set_names order. This guarantees exact total and deterministic quotas. For each quota, empirical-resample a valid row with replacement using rng.choice; sample centre components independently with rng.uniform(xmin, xmax), rng.uniform(ymin, ymax), rng.uniform(zmin, zmax). Use sampled trace azimuth as geological strike (degrees to radians) and sampled dip (degrees to radians); PorePy right-hand rule implies dip direction, so v1 neither reads nor emits dip direction. Create circular EllipticalFracture values: axis=sampled trace length / 2 and major_axis_angle=0. Return a string whose first row is the six-value cuboid domain, followed by one eight-field row per generated fracture. The function need not call a separate CSV validator. Guarantee centres only, not disk containment. Validate finite strictly increasing bounds and count > 0 before sampling. No PorePy import/dependency, parametric distribution sampling, or new configuration classes.
acceptance_criteria: With a seeded numpy.random.default_rng passed twice, identical input yields byte-identical CSV. Tests prove domain is the first six-field line; each later row parses to eight finite numeric fields with equal positive axes; exact output row count equals fracture_count; quota allocation uses usable observation count and largest-remainder/original-name tie break; sampled axis is one half of a valid source length; strike is a source azimuth in radians; dip is a source dip in radians; every centre lies inside supplied bounds; invalid count/bounds fail clearly. Test manual and automatic set labels through 861 extraction. Run nix develop -c pytest tests/interop/test_porepy.py -q. Run nix develop -c prek run --all-files. Before closing: br close with test evidence, br sync --flush-only, git add -f .beads/issues.jsonl plus source/test files, and commit --no-gpg-sign with this bead id.

title: Correct PorePy 3D semi-axis semantics
description: Correct existing 3D PorePy export semantics in fractopo/interop/porepy.py, with tests in tests/interop/test_porepy.py. PorePy network_from_csv elliptic rows are CENTER_X,CENTER_Y,CENTER_Z,MAJOR_AXIS,MINOR_AXIS,MAJOR_AXIS_ANGLE,STRIKE_ANGLE,DIP_ANGLE; PorePy EllipticFracture stores major/minor values as radius-like semi-axes (r1/r2). fractopo input lengths are full observed trace/diameter lengths: EllipticalFracture.from_linestring_and_orientation and .from_structural_measurement must write major_axis == minor_axis == length / 2. Preserve centre and angle behavior. Do not add a general 3D CSV validator: every v1 export owns its simple row formatting and focused tests can parse/assert its 8 numeric fields. Do not import/install PorePy; the project intentionally has no PorePy runtime dependency. Do not alter 2D behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Tests prove both existing 3D exporters emit exactly eight numeric fields per fracture and output half the supplied trace/measurement length in both axis fields, retaining existing centres and radian angle conversions. Update affected doctest output to semi-axis values. Run nix develop -c pytest tests/interop/test_porepy.py -q. Run nix develop -c prek run --all-files. Before closing: br close with test evidence, br sync --flush-only, git add -f .beads/issues.jsonl plus source/test files, and commit --no-gpg-sign with this bead id.
